summary: Candidate runtime is deployable on the same production path (entrypoint + CMD override to sleep infinity + dataops-dsh-service): DSH 0.2.3-alpha.2 at the required path, 26 profile bundles, gateway sidecar starts, cold ready 43.6s and warm ready 4.3s, DSH RSS 334,548KB, writable layer 733kB. Image 11.9GB vs production 13.2GB. One pre-existing image-default-CMD defect was reproduced: CMD references missing /opt/dataops-runtime/src/daemon.mjs; the production image has the same defect and the running production container overrides CMD, so it is not a candidate regression, but the image cannot boot on its default CMD alone.

checks.detail: Symlink resolves to ../@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js; the same version is reported by dsh inside the running runtime container.
Image template and first-boot runtime volume both report 26 bundles / 28 @sparkelf dirs / 422 @deepseek-ai dirs. web.log has 0 'skipping profile bundle' lines.
Combined gateway log reports 'running: web, sdk'; SDK listener owns 0.0.0.0:43118 inside the container (not published).

checks.error: Error: Cannot find module '/opt/dataops-runtime/src/daemon.mjs' (code MODULE_NOT_FOUND, Node.js v26.13.1)
checks.detail: The same default CMD fails identically on dataops-ai-workspace:final-20261125-sdkfix. Older images dataops-ai-workspace:delivery-20261123-amd64 and dataops-ai-workspace:final-20261124-0032 also lack daemon.mjs. The running dataops-ai-admin container overrides CMD to '... exec sleep infinity', so this path is not used in the deployment.

checks.command: docker run -d --name b09a-candidate-runtime-20261126 --env-file /tmp/b09a-env -e DATAOPS_DSH_PORT=13080 -v b09a-candidate-workspace-20261126:/workspace dataops-ai-workspace-candidate:local /bin/sh -lc 'exec sleep infinity'
checks.actual: entrypoint active; independent sshd listener; combined workspace-gateway process; dataops-dsh-service start returned state=running, ready=true, pid=1304, port=13080
checks.detail: The CMD override matches the running production container's Cmd. No host port was published.

Cold start copied the 805MB profile template to the fresh volume. One immediate status call right after start returned transient state=starting; after 5-10s it was stably running/ready. Warm restart (same volume) ready in 4.3s.
401 means the route is registered behind browser authentication; no 404/5xx. The service readiness check uses the model-sync route and reported ready=true.

dsh RSS is 23.8MB below the 358MB baseline; combined gateway+dsh RSS is within 1.1MB of baseline. The combined gateway process alone is 24.9MB above the baseline 44.9MB snapshot; treat that as an observation, not a gate failure.
Measured after a cold start and a warm stop/start; the 805MB profile lives on the fresh named volume, not the writable layer.

checks.actual: PortBindings={}, NetworkSettings.Ports={}, network=bridge; production container remained running with unchanged StartedAt; host listeners 127.0.0.1:3080 and 0.0.0.0:3000 unchanged.
checks.detail: Temporary container and volume were removed after measurement; env file containing secrets was deleted.

deviations: Used a fresh named volume b09a-candidate-workspace-20261126 at /workspace instead of the production volume dataops-ai-admin-dsh-run, so production profile/session data could not be modified. Same mount destination and same env set were used, minus DATAOPS_DSH_PROFILE_SOURCE_REF/DATAOPS_DSH_SOURCE_REF/DATAOPS_DSH_PORT.
DSH listened on loopback port 13080 inside the container instead of 3080; no port was published, so host 3000/3080 were untouched.

Seeded a random 64-character owner token at /run/dataops-workspace/internal-token (nobody:nogroup, 0640) to unblock the sidecar's documented wait. The production container has the same 64-byte file; in this isolated test the platform helper/daemon path that provisions it is unavailable because of the missing daemon.mjs.
Used CMD override sleep infinity to match the running dataops-ai-admin container. The image default CMD was tested separately and fails (see checks.default-entrypoint-cmd).
Gateway backend authentication with the synthetic owner token was not asserted; the gateway process and listeners were verified, not the portal end-to-end handshake.
